title: Why Derivatives Trading Just Got More 'Cash-Heavy' in India
description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) recently tightened rules for bank guarantees used in derivatives trading. Now, banks must fully back these guarantees with col.

faq.a: A bank guarantee is a promise from a bank to cover a financial obligation if their client defaults. It acts as a form of security.

Derivatives are financial contracts whose value is derived from an underlying asset, like stocks, commodities, or currencies. They are used for managing risk (hedging) or for making speculative bets on future price movements.
Collateral refers to assets that a borrower pledges to a lender as security for a loan. If the borrower fails to repay, the lender can seize the collateral.

faq.q: Why did the RBI make this change?
faq.a: The RBI introduced these tighter rules to reduce the risk for banks that issue guarantees for derivatives trading. By requiring more cash collateral, banks are better protected if a trading firm defaults.

faq.q: Does this mean derivatives trading will stop?
faq.a: No, derivatives trading will continue. However, the new rules are expected to make it more capital-intensive and reduce the amount of leverage available to trading firms, which has already led to a dip in trading volumes.
